description: Shared RabbitMQ management-API contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server (server issue #499). Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/rabbitmq_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_rabbitmq.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip (only the HTTP transport is mocked -- a fake session dispatches each scenario's 'responses' per endpoint, feeding status codes + bodies back through the real _request classification and normalization). rabbitmq_metrics(**scenario['config']['rabbitmq']) must equal scenario['payload']['rabbitmq']. The server's spec/requests/api_collect_rabbitmq_spec.rb posts scenario['payload']['rabbitmq'] under data['rabbitmq'] through /collect and asserts Ingesters::Agent ingests each shape (reachable envelope / unreachable envelope). 'config' and 'responses' are agent-side inputs the server ignores. Change the payload shape only in lockstep across both repos, keeping the two copies byte-identical.
_agent_min_version_note: RabbitMQ has NO server version gate (no FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS entry -- purely config-driven, rabbitmq_enabled defaults false), so this number is free and nothing gates on it. 1.14.2 slots into the in-flight 1.14.x collector cluster (Docker image-inventory PR #102 = 1.14.0; TSDB PR #108 / issue #103 = 1.14.1; then RabbitMQ = 1.14.2), between those and Memcached's 1.14.4. Same cede-the-taken-slot discipline as PHP-FPM #97 (which ceded 1.13.0 to Ceph). The maintainer may re-slot on merge; nothing depends on the exact value.
envelope_contract: data['rabbitmq'] is ALWAYS one of two envelopes and the server MUST branch on 'reachable'. (a) reachable:true = a trustworthy tick -> {version, node{...}, queues_total, queues[...]}. (b) reachable:false = a dead broker OR a partially-fetched queue list -> {error_type, error_message} with NO 'queues'/'node'/'version' key. On reachable:false the server MUST NOT ingest queue rows, prune rabbitmq_queues rows, or auto-resolve rabbitmq_queue_backlog incidents: a broker that is merely unreachable (or a page that failed midway) is not 'every queue deleted', and treating it as recovery is a false-resolve bug. This is the postgresql/mysql reachability posture, NOT the php_fpm null contract -- a dead broker on a control plane IS the signal, so it rides the payload rather than collapsing to null.
bounded_queues_contract: 'queues' is BOUNDED: the union of top-N by 'messages' and top-N by 'messages_unacked', plus any 'include_queues' names (the server echoes trigger watch lists there so a below-cap watched queue keeps updating). 'queues_total' carries the broker's TRUE queue count for the collected scope (the SNMP interface_count precedent) even when far more queues exist than are shipped -- see the cap_overflow scenario (queues_total 184 > 3 shipped). The unacked dimension is NOT redundant with 'messages' (which already includes unacked): a small queue whose consumers are stuck (high unacked, low total) can miss top-N-by-messages yet is exactly the 'consumers == 0 with depth > 0' case the trigger fires on -- see the 'dlq.orders' queue in cap_overflow, surfaced only by the unacked sort.

field_contract.node: Local node health from /api/nodes (the node serving the management request, selected by overview.node on a cluster).
field_contract.node.mem_alarm: Memory high-watermark alarm (bool). true blocks publishers cluster-wide -- a direct outage predictor.
field_contract.node.fd_used / node.fd_total: File descriptors in use / limit -- socket + file headroom.
field_contract.queues_total: TRUE count of queues in the collected scope, independent of how many rows are shipped (bounded array). Server uses it for a 'N queues not shown' indicator.
field_contract.queue.vhost / queue.name: The per-queue entity key (a queue name is unique within a vhost).
field_contract.queue.messages: Total ready + unacknowledged messages -- the backlog DEPTH the trigger reads.
field_contract.queue.messages_unacked: RabbitMQ messages_unacknowledged -- delivered-but-not-acked; a stuck-consumer signal.
field_contract.queue.consumers: Consumer count. 0 with messages > 0 is the zero-consumer backlog the trigger fires on.
field_contract.queue.publish_total: message_stats.publish -- RAW cumulative publishes; the server rate()s it. OMITTED when the queue has no message_stats (idle, never published). Never diff/reset agent-side.
field_contract.queue.deliver_total: message_stats.deliver_get -- RAW cumulative deliveries/gets; the server rate()s it. OMITTED with publish_total when message_stats is absent.

healthy.description: A healthy single-node broker. 'notifications' is a zero-consumer backlog queue (consumers 0, messages 12000) -- the trigger's headline case. 'orders' is a normally-drained queue. 'logs' is idle with NO message_stats, so publish_total/deliver_total are OMITTED (not null). No node alarms. Both ranked pages return the same three queues, so the union dedups to three in messages order.

node_mem_alarm.description: Memory high-watermark alarm raised (mem_alarm true) with fd/socket usage climbing toward the limits -- the node-health half of the feature. Publishers are blocked cluster-wide; the server drives a node alarm from this independent of any per-queue trigger. One queue keeps the payload complete.

unreachable.description: The broker is down: the first request (/api/overview) fails at the network layer. Collapses to the unreachable envelope with error_type connection_refused and NO queues/node/version key -- the server skips ingestion so open backlog incidents cannot false-resolve. error_message is the agent-generated exception string (the server treats it as opaque; only error_type is semantic).

auth_failure.description: Wrong credentials: /api/overview returns HTTP 401. Collapses to the unreachable envelope with error_type auth_failed -- the server routes this to a config_error (fix the credentials) rather than a broker outage. NO queues key.

cap_overflow.description: A broker with 184 queues, of which only a bounded set is shipped: queues_total 184 > 3 rows (the SNMP interface_count precedent). Also pins the ranked UNION: the messages page returns the two deepest queues; the unacked page surfaces 'dlq.orders' -- a low-depth (300) but fully-stuck (unacked 300, consumers 0, deliver 0) dead-letter queue that misses top-N-by-messages yet is the exact zero-consumer-backlog case the trigger exists for. The union is [messages page..., then unacked-only additions], deduped by (vhost, name).

include_below_cap.description: A 184-queue broker where the two ranked pages surface only the two deepest queues. 'dlq.watch' is a stuck dead-letter queue (consumers 0, all unacked) that has dropped below the ranked cap, but the server echoes it in include_queues so it is force-fetched by exact identity and APPENDED to the array -- keeping its row alive so its open rabbitmq_queue_backlog incident can still resolve. Pins the include_queues wiring (config -> single-queue GET -> appended row) and that queues_total (184) still reflects the broker total, not the shipped count (3).
